audit: R3 independent relationship-evidence and historical-map audit
sampling: Risk-based purposive sample. All three newly encoded documented-transmission edges plus two new cross-strand comparisons. Not a random quality estimate; unchanged accepted claims reopened only as necessary to test new comparison links. No cross-strand causal edges will be invented.

selected.selection_reason: Named H4-to-K1 replication is a rare newly encoded historical transmission and has potentially conflicting completion/delivery chronology.

record.qualification: Named replication by another maker; not a cost-effective serial-production claim.

scope.configuration: Kendall's commissioned H4 copy leading to K1 in 1769

record.dispute: Exact access/instruction sequence not independently reconstructed from Board papers.

selected.selection_reason: New documented-transmission label on apprenticeship could confuse observed pedagogy with an independently reconstructed historical diffusion path.

record.qualification: Observed pedagogy passes practical work opportunities through supervision; no exclusivity of apprenticeship.

selected.selection_reason: New cross-strand link between roads/lorry agency and rail history is the closest new transport integration; must distinguish overlapping evidence and complement/competition from falsification of rail effects.

record.question: How does African road/lorry initiative change the interpretation of the Ghana railway episode?
record.useful_similarities: Same southern cocoa economy, overlapping transport periods, farmers and alternative routes; both separate local response from the priorities of colonial planners.
record.important_differences: MOB-C04 reports spatial railway effects and persistence to 2000; GHA-C01 asks who made roads, entered haulage and controlled land/labour. Their outcome and actor units differ.
record.evidence_comparability: Additional historical actor/process evidence is neither a replication nor a matched substitute for the rail spatial design. No combined modal-share series is built because early transport summaries require reconciliation.
record.connections_nonindependence: GHA-S05 is exactly the manuscript recorded as MOB-S08 and directly cites GHA-S01 (Austin 2007) plus Hill (1963). Austin’s transport discussion draws partly on Heap and colonial reports. Historical references are shared, while the rail study’s assembled spatial data and estimator are distinct evidence.
record.omitted_countercases: Matched African-built versus government-built routes; failed roads/operators; unbuilt connections with comparable demand; original Cardinall/Luntinen series and rail-study data/code reanalysis.
record.conclusion_limit: Local road and enterprise agency prevents a passive-recipient narrative but does not logically invalidate rail effects or prove universal consent. Parent owns integration of this cross-contribution reference.

selected.selection_reason: New cross-strand cross-period textile link could smuggle continuity or causality across 1949, or count the same underlying source twice.

record.question: When household textiles persist alongside factories, does useful task fit, restricted substitution or unequal allocation of labour explain the continuation?
record.useful_similarities: Separable spinning/weaving/clothing tasks, household production alongside industrial textiles, and gendered work. Similar visible persistence can conceal different feasible choices and beneficiaries.
record.important_differences: IND-C07 is c.1870–1949 and includes market integration through factory yarn; CTX-C01 is 1949–1980 with its own mid-1950s procurement/collectivisation institutions and local retrospective sample. Product, place, date and institutions are not held constant.
record.evidence_comparability: IND uses inherited historical background and an attributed interwar national output estimate; CTX centres original interviews/archival interpretation from three Guanzhong villages. No pooled denominator, matched before/after effect or common output-share series is defensible.
record.connections_nonindependence: Direct work-level dependence: CTX-S01 and IND-S15 are the EXACT SAME Eyferth2012 article, using different sections and underlying evidence. The histories are temporally connected, not independent replications. CTX-S03 note49 inherits Eyferth2012/2015 for cloth access, and both draw on Hershatter/Gao for wider rural work; original-record overlap beyond named citations is unknown.
record.omitted_countercases: Matched households with sufficient cash and equivalent factory cloth; non-cotton or nonweaving regions; profitable commercial producers with documented control of proceeds; households where men shared textile work; the same households through late-1970s exit.
record.conclusion_limit: The earlier hybrid claim survives. The later episode adds concrete constrained-access and unpaid-labour routes, so persistence alone cannot establish preference, efficiency, consent, welfare or an accessible paid repair/adaptation role. No backward projection or national causal weighting follows.
